prompts.body_text: Can the need to enter the confined space be avoided? (Consider remote controls, video camera, or inspection hatches.)
Can the confined space be permanently re-classified by removing the enclosed nature?
Can the confined space be permanently re-classified by removing the specified hazard(s) that make it a confined space?
Can the confined space be temporarily re-classified by forced ventilation at a rate that would make an unsafe atmosphere impossible?
If forced ventilation fails, is there sufficient time for a safe evacuation?
Has a specific risk assessment been completed for the confined space?
Has the risk assessment considered all conditions of operation, including abnormal and temporary conditions such as welding?
Has the risk assessment considered risks created by the planned work (e.g. burning, welding, static discharges)?
Has a specific safe working procedure (safe system of work) been prepared and is it relevant to the planned activity?
Does the safe working procedure specify the measures to be taken in the event of an emergency?
Has a Confined Space Permit been raised, including any control measures specified in this checklist?
Has a suitable warning sign been posted to identify the confined space?
Has the confined space been secured (e.g. barrier, guard, or gate) to deter unauthorised access?
Have fixed gas detectors or low oxygen monitors been provided and are they in a suitable location?

prompts.body_text: Are gas detectors adequately maintained and calibrated?
Can the confined space be ventilated naturally to reduce unsafe atmosphere risk (e.g. by opening or removing doors or hatches)?
Have fixed ventilation provisions been made?
Is fixed ventilation maintained and tested periodically?
Have cameras been fitted to monitor persons inside the confined space if identified as a control?
Is there adequate communication between persons inside and outside the confined space?
Is sufficient ventilation available? (Do not force oxygen into the space—it can create an explosive atmosphere.)
Is lighting inside the confined space adequate?
Can ambient temperature in the confined space be controlled or monitored to prevent excessive heat for operatives?
Has adequate access been provided for safe entry into the confined space?
Are walkways and access platforms to the confined space opening safe to use?
Is access size sufficient for PPE and emergency BA? (Min 575mm square for BA emergencies; 457mm dia round or 457×410mm rectangular otherwise.)
Is sufficient access equipment (tripod, full body harness, winch) available for access/egress?
Have all persons who manage or enter the confined space received training, demonstrated competency, and been authorised?
Are individuals of suitable build and fitness where physical constraints were highlighted in the risk assessment?
Has the site appointed sufficient competent persons to issue permits and supervise confined space activities?
Are all employees/contractors aware a Permit to Work is required before anyone enters?
Are all employees/contractors aware of procedures when the task, environment, or method of work changes?

extracted.title: Confined Spaces

items.headline: What is a confined space?
items.body: Any space of an enclosed nature where there is a risk of death or injury from hazardous substances or dangerous conditions (e.g. lack of oxygen). Typical features include limited ways in and out, hazardous substances or atmosphere, and risk of being trapped, engulfed, or drowned.

items.headline: Examples of confined spaces
items.body: Examples include grain silos, wood pellet stores, sewers, areas with intentionally reduced oxygen such as fruit stores, and storage tanks.

items.headline: Avoid entry unless absolutely necessary
items.body: Confined spaces are not designed to be worked in for long periods. Avoid entering a confined space unless you are trained and equipped to do so and it is absolutely necessary.

items.headline: Hazards in confined spaces
items.body: Hazards include lack of oxygen (suffocation), fire and explosion risk, build-up of toxic substances, and physical hazards such as noise, extreme temperatures, mechanical hazards, falls, electrocution, and machinery.

items.headline: Before entering: assessment, training, and testing
items.body: Ensure a risk assessment has been carried out, you have received specific training, and atmospheric testing has been carried out.

items.headline: Isolate and ventilate the space
items.body: Isolate the space by turning off gas, power, etc. and ventilate for at least 15 minutes. Ensure all flammable or toxic materials or substances have been safely removed.

items.headline: Team size and buddy system
items.body: Ensure at least three people are present (buddy system) unless rescue is possible with an external winch and the person in the confined space is permanently attached to a rescue line connected to the winch, when two is acceptable.

items.headline: Medical fitness and permit to work
items.body: Ensure you are medically fit and that a permit to work is in place and signed, authorising the type of work. Ensure you understand all precautions to be taken.

items.headline: Understand your permit conditions
items.body: Before entry, confirm who is allowed in, what barriers, warning signs, and covers are needed, what PPE must be worn, whether ventilation and atmospheric monitoring is required, rescue and emergency procedures, means of communication, required safety and monitoring equipment, how long the permit lasts, and any special instructions or precautions.

items.headline: Legislation and guidance
items.body: Relevant legislation includes the Health and Safety at Work etc Act 1974, the Confined Spaces Regulations 1997, the Management of Health and Safety at Work Regulations 1999, and the Personal Protective Equipment at Work Regulations 1992 (as amended). Guidance: INDG258 — Safe Working in Confined Spaces.

key_messages: Do not enter a confined space unless you are trained, equipped, and entry is absolutely necessary.
Before entry, complete a risk assessment, atmospheric testing, isolation, and ventilation for at least 15 minutes.
Ensure a signed permit to work is in place and you understand all its conditions, including rescue and communication arrangements.
At least three people must be present unless an external winch rescue setup with a permanently attached rescue line allows two.
Confined spaces can kill through lack of oxygen, fire or explosion, toxic substances, and physical hazards — treat every entry as high risk.
